Summary: UC1 - Smart Treatment Journey Management
Description: Show each member the appropriate next medical step, based on existing medical information, tests, referrals, appointments and missing documents.

Summary: Display the member's treatment journey timeline
Description: As a member, I want to see my treatment journey as a timeline, so that I know what has been done and what my next step is. The system will show the member a clear timeline of their personal care process, including tests, appointments, referrals, missing documents, prescriptions and open treatment steps. Goal: help the member understand which stage they are at, what has already been done and what they need to do next.
Acceptance Criteria: Display treatment steps in chronological order | Show a status for each step: completed, pending, missing information or action required | Highlight the next recommended action | Refresh displayed information from relevant health-plan systems

Summary: Define the treatment timeline structure
Description: Define the logical structure of the medical timeline, including event types, statuses and display order.

Summary: Define medical event types displayed on the timeline
Description: Define the events shown on the timeline, such as tests, appointments, referrals, documents and prescriptions.

Summary: Define status labels for each treatment step
Description: Define step statuses such as Completed, Pending, Missing information and Action required.

Summary: Define display order by date and treatment sequence
Description: Set the order in which events are displayed, by date and by treatment sequence.

Summary: Develop the member timeline screen
Description: Implement a screen that presents the member's medical journey clearly.

Summary: Design responsive timeline layouts for mobile and web
Description: Design a timeline layout adapted to both the mobile app and the website.

Summary: Connect the timeline to tests, appointments, referrals and documents
Description: Connect the screen to the relevant medical data sources.

Summary: Highlight the member's recommended next step
Description: Show the next action the member needs to take in their care process.

Summary: Medical events appear in the wrong chronological order
Description: Simulated defect scenario: treatment steps are displayed in the wrong order on the timeline.
Expected Result: Events are listed chronologically: test -> referral -> appointment.
Simulated Actual Result: Events appear out of order (e.g. the March test is shown after the May appointment).

Summary: Display missing tests and documents before an appointment
Description: As a member, I want to see which tests or documents are missing before an appointment, so that I arrive prepared and my care is not delayed. The system will check which tests, documents or referrals are required before a medical appointment and show the member a clear list of what is missing. Goal: prevent members from arriving at an appointment without required information, which can delay diagnosis or treatment.
Acceptance Criteria: Identify required documents and tests according to appointment type | Compare required items with the existing medical record | Clearly display outstanding requirements | Show a readiness message if no information is missing

Summary: Define appointment-specific test and document requirements
Description: Define which documents and tests are required before each type of appointment.

Summary: Identify required documents by specialty or examination type
Description: Create a list of required documents by medical field and service type.

Summary: Identify tests that must be completed before appointments
Description: Determine which tests must be completed before a specific appointment.

Summary: Review requirements with a clinical stakeholder
Description: Review and approve the requirements with a qualified clinical professional.

Summary: Develop missing-test and missing-document detection
Description: Implement a mechanism that compares appointment requirements with the data already in the medical record.

Summary: Compare appointment requirements against the medical record
Description: Check whether the required documents and tests already exist in the system.

Summary: Present outstanding requirements clearly to the member
Description: Present missing items to the member in a simple, understandable way.

Summary: Display a readiness message when nothing is missing
Description: Tell the member they are ready for the appointment and no actions are pending.

Summary: An existing medical document is incorrectly flagged as missing
Description: Simulated defect scenario: the system does not recognize a document that already exists in the medical record.
Expected Result: The letter is recognized; if nothing else is missing, the 'You're ready' message is shown.
Simulated Actual Result: The letter is still listed as missing.

Summary: Display outstanding treatment steps to authorized clinicians
Description: As a physician, I want to see whether my patient has completed the treatment steps required of them, so that I can follow up and keep continuity of care. The system will let the care provider see the patient's open treatment steps, including completed actions, actions not yet completed and existing gaps. Goal: give the physician or care provider a quick status picture and improve continuity of care.
Acceptance Criteria: Show outstanding treatment steps for each relevant patient | Display an up-to-date status for each step | Identify missing tests, referrals and documents | Allow access only to authorized care professionals

Summary: Specify the clinician's treatment-step tracking screen
Description: Define the structure of the screen that shows a patient's treatment steps to the care provider.

Summary: Define the patient information shown to each clinician
Description: Determine the medical and treatment data shown on the screen.

Summary: Define statuses for outstanding treatment steps
Description: Define statuses such as Open, Completed, Missing information and Awaiting approval.

Summary: Specify viewing permissions by clinical role
Description: Determine who may view the information, based on clinical role and care relationship.

Summary: Develop the display of pending patient treatment steps
Description: Implement the open-treatment-steps view for the care provider.

Summary: Display a list of outstanding treatment steps
Description: Show all steps that have not yet been completed.

Summary: Show missing tests, referrals and documents
Description: Show missing information that could delay further treatment.

Summary: Allow an authorized clinician to mark a step complete
Description: Allow the care provider to update the status of a treatment step.

Summary: A clinician can see treatment steps for an unrelated patient
Description: Simulated defect scenario (critical, access control): a care provider can view the treatment steps of a patient outside their responsibility.
Expected Result: Only patients under Physician A's care are listed.
Simulated Actual Result: The list includes a patient with no care relationship to Physician A.

Summary: Notify members about incomplete medical actions
Description: As a member, I want to be notified when a medical action is still incomplete, so that I don't miss a test, document or appointment. The system will notify the member when medical actions are still incomplete - for example a test, a document upload, booking an appointment or renewing a referral. Goal: help members complete treatment steps on time and reduce delays in the care process.
Acceptance Criteria: Detect medical actions that remain incomplete | Deliver notifications through an appropriate channel: push, SMS or email | Explain which action the patient should take | Prevent duplicate notifications for the same action

Summary: Define triggers for medical-action notifications
Description: Define the situations in which the system sends the member a notification.

Summary: Identify incomplete actions that trigger a reminder
Description: Define triggering actions, e.g. a test not performed, a missing document or an appointment not booked.

Summary: Specify notification frequency
Description: Determine when, and how many times, a notification is sent.

Summary: Define safeguards against duplicate notifications
Description: Prevent unnecessary repeat sending of the same notification.

Summary: Develop member notification delivery
Description: Implement notification delivery to the member over several channels.

Summary: Implement push notifications
Description: Implement in-app push notifications for incomplete medical actions.

Summary: Implement email and SMS notifications
Description: Implement Email and SMS as additional notification channels.

Summary: Verify notifications are delivered to members
Description: Verify that the notification is received with correct, clear content.

Summary: Duplicate reminders are sent for the same incomplete action
Description: Simulated defect scenario: duplicate notifications are sent for the same incomplete action.
Expected Result: One notification is sent, per the defined frequency rule.
Simulated Actual Result: The member receives the same notification twice.

Summary: UC2 - Smart Appointment Scheduling
Description: Let members book a suitable appointment based on medical need, existing referral, clinician availability and treatment stage.

Summary: Recommend an appropriate appointment type based on medical context
Description: As a member, I want a recommendation for which type of appointment to book, so that I book the right appointment the first time. The system will recommend which type of appointment the member should book, based on their medical condition, existing referrals, test results and current treatment stage. Goal: direct the member to the most suitable appointment and prevent wrong or irrelevant bookings.
Acceptance Criteria: Identify a suitable appointment type from the available medical information | Display the recommendation in a patient-friendly manner | Warn when a referral is required before booking | Connect the recommendation to the treatment journey timeline

Summary: Define business rules for appointment recommendations
Description: Define the business rules by which the system recommends a suitable appointment type.

Summary: Map medical needs to suitable appointment types
Description: Map medical situations to appointment types such as family doctor, specialist or test.

Summary: Define when a referral is required before booking
Description: Determine when a referral is required before an appointment can be booked.

Summary: Write explanatory messages for members
Description: Write a clear explanation of the reason for each recommendation.

Summary: Develop the appointment-type recommendation workflow
Description: Implement a mechanism that shows the member the appropriate appointment type.

Summary: Retrieve relevant context from the medical record
Description: Use test results, referrals and existing medical information as input.

Summary: Display the recommended appointment type
Description: Show the recommendation clearly on the member's screen.

Summary: Link recommendations to the treatment journey timeline
Description: Add the recommendation as part of the overall care process (timeline).

Summary: A specialist appointment is recommended without the required referral
Description: Simulated defect scenario: a recommendation is shown that does not meet process requirements (a required referral is missing).
Expected Result: The system warns that a referral is required and does not offer the specialist appointment as bookable.
Simulated Actual Result: A specialist appointment is recommended without any referral warning.

Summary: Display available clinicians and appointments by referral, specialty and location
Description: As a member, I want to see available clinicians that match my referral and location, so that I can choose a suitable slot quickly. The system will show the member a list of available clinicians and appointments according to referral type, medical field, the member's location and slot availability. Goal: let the member choose a suitable appointment quickly and easily.
Acceptance Criteria: Display only appointment slots matching the referral or clinical need | Allow filters by location, specialty and date | Display clinician, facility, date and time details | Show a clear message if no appointments are available

Summary: Connect to the health plan appointment system
Description: Build an integration that retrieves available appointments and clinicians.

Summary: Review the API for retrieving available appointment slots
Description: Verify that available slots can be retrieved from the appointment system's API.

Summary: Retrieve clinicians by specialty
Description: Retrieve clinicians by medical field or specialty.

Summary: Retrieve availability by location and date
Description: Retrieve appointments by geographic area and preferred date.

Summary: Develop the clinician and appointment availability view
Description: Implement an appointment selection screen with a list of clinicians and availability.

Summary: Display available clinicians and appointment slots
Description: Display each available slot with its date, time, clinic and clinician name.

Summary: Add filters for location, specialty and date
Description: Add search and filtering of available appointments by location, medical field and date.

Summary: Show an informative empty state when no appointments are available
Description: Show an appropriate message and suggest a next action.

Summary: Appointment slots do not match the member's referral type
Description: Simulated defect scenario: appointments that do not match the member's referral type are displayed.
Simulated Actual Result: Slots from unrelated specialties are also shown.

Summary: Book an appointment directly from a system recommendation
Description: As a member, I want to book directly from the recommendation I received, so that I don't have to start a new search. The system will let the member book directly from the recommendation shown, without moving to unrelated screens or searching again manually. Goal: a continuous flow - recommendation -> slot selection -> confirmation -> care-process update.
Acceptance Criteria: Allow selection of an appointment from recommended options | Save the appointment after confirmation | Add the appointment to the treatment timeline | Display a booking confirmation to the patient

Summary: Develop booking flow from the system recommendation
Description: Implement a direct transition from the system recommendation to choosing a suitable appointment.

Summary: Add a booking action to the recommendation view
Description: Add a clear action that allows booking directly from the recommendation.

Summary: Display appointment details before confirmation
Description: Show date, time, clinician and location before final confirmation.

Summary: Save the selected appointment in the booking system
Description: Save the appointment in the health plan's appointment system.

Summary: Update the treatment journey after appointment booking
Description: Update the timeline and treatment steps once the appointment is booked.

Summary: Add the booked appointment to the medical timeline
Description: Show the new appointment as part of the medical timeline.

Summary: Update the treatment-step status after booking
Description: Change the step status from 'Awaiting booking' to 'Appointment booked'.

Summary: Display booking confirmation to the member
Description: Show a confirmation message once the booking is complete.

Summary: Booked appointment is not added to the member's timeline
Description: Simulated defect scenario: the appointment system and the timeline are not synchronized after booking.
Expected Result: The new appointment appears on the timeline and the step status changes to 'Appointment booked'.
Simulated Actual Result: The booking is saved in the appointment system but does not appear on the timeline.

Summary: Send booking confirmations and appointment reminders
Description: As a member, I want a confirmation and a reminder after booking, so that I remember the appointment and arrive prepared. The system will send the member a confirmation after booking and a reminder before the appointment. Goal: reduce missed appointments and make sure the member arrives with the required documents and tests.
Acceptance Criteria: Send a confirmation after an appointment is booked | Include the date, time, location and clinician or service | Send a reminder before the appointment | Include missing-document information when relevant

Summary: Specify booking confirmation and reminder messages
Description: Define the structure and content of the messages sent to the member.

Summary: Define required content for booking confirmations
Description: Determine the details included in the confirmation: date, time, location and clinician name.

Summary: Define when pre-appointment reminders should be sent
Description: Determine when the reminder is sent before the appointment.

Summary: Include missing-document information in reminders
Description: Add information about missing documents or tests before the appointment.

Summary: Develop booking confirmation and reminder delivery
Description: Implement sending of confirmation and reminder messages to the member.

Summary: Send a confirmation after booking
Description: Send a confirmation message immediately after booking.

Summary: Send a reminder before the scheduled appointment
Description: Send an automatic reminder before the appointment.

Summary: Verify the date, time and location in notification content
Description: Verify that the message includes all appointment details.

Summary: Booking confirmation omits the appointment date and time
Description: Simulated defect scenario: essential appointment details are missing from the confirmation message.
Expected Result: The message includes date, time, location and clinician/service.
Simulated Actual Result: The message is sent without the date and time.

Summary: UC3 - Digital Medical Record Management
Description: Give members and clinicians consolidated, up-to-date and clear medical information: tests, documents, referrals, medications, appointments and history.

Summary: Display a consolidated digital medical record to the member
Description: As a member, I want to view my medical record in one place, so that I don't have to search across separate screens. The system will present a consolidated digital medical record that includes relevant information such as tests, documents, referrals, appointments, medications and follow-up data. Goal: let the member see their medical information in one place, clearly and accessibly.
Acceptance Criteria: Allow patients to view their consolidated medical record | Organize medical information into clear categories | Make the information easy to understand | Update the record from relevant health-plan systems

Summary: Define the member medical record information architecture
Description: Define the structure of the medical record and the categories shown to the member.

Summary: Define categories within the digital medical record
Description: Define categories such as tests, documents, referrals, medications and appointments.

Summary: Define member-visible information for each category
Description: Determine the data shown in each medical category.

Summary: Specify a clear and accessible presentation of medical information
Description: Plan an accessible, clear display for the user.

Summary: Develop the consolidated member record screen
Description: Implement a screen that shows all of the member's medical information in one place.

Summary: Develop the tests and documents section
Description: Display tests and medical documents in the member's record.

Summary: Develop the referrals, appointments and medications section
Description: Display information on referrals, appointments and active medications.

Summary: Connect the member record to relevant health-plan data
Description: Retrieve information from the health plan's medical information systems.

Summary: Some medical record categories do not load for the member
Description: Simulated defect scenario: not all medical record categories are displayed to the member.
Expected Result: All categories (tests, documents, referrals, medications, appointments) load.
Simulated Actual Result: Some categories do not load and appear empty.

Summary: Display a consolidated clinical overview for the care team
Description: As a physician, I want a consolidated clinical overview of my patient, so that I can prepare quickly without switching between systems. The system will give the care provider a consolidated clinical overview of the patient, including up-to-date tests, referrals, medications, documents and open treatment steps. Goal: help the care provider understand the patient's status quickly and make treatment decisions more efficiently.
Acceptance Criteria: Present key medical information to an authorized clinician | Show outstanding treatment steps and missing items | Show recent tests and documents | Restrict access to authorized users

Summary: Specify the clinician-facing patient overview
Description: Define the structure of the clinical overview screen for the care provider.

Summary: Define key patient information for the overview
Description: Select the key data shown to the physician or care provider.

Summary: Define how outstanding treatment steps will appear
Description: Include open treatment steps in the overview screen.

Summary: Define how recent tests and documents will appear
Description: Show only up-to-date, relevant medical information.

Summary: Develop the clinician-facing patient overview screen
Description: Implement a screen that gives the care provider a consolidated clinical overview.

Summary: Display basic patient details
Description: Display the patient's basic details in the clinical overview.

Summary: Display key medical information
Description: Display important medical information in an organized way.

Summary: Enable access to medical documents from the overview
Description: Open medical documents from within the overview.

Summary: An authorized clinician cannot open a patient's medical document
Description: Simulated defect scenario: an authorized care provider cannot open a patient's medical document.
Simulated Actual Result: An access error is shown, although the physician is authorized.

Summary: Organize medical tests and documents by category
Description: As a member, I want to see test results and medical documents organized by category, so that I can find a specific item easily. The system will present test results and medical documents to the member and care provider, organized by category, document type and date. Goal: enable fast retrieval of medical information and avoid confusion between documents.
Acceptance Criteria: Organize results and documents by category | Allow filtering by document type, date or medical specialty | Display each item's name, date and status | Allow opening a document or result from the list

Summary: Define document categories and filtering requirements
Description: Define the category structure, search and filtering for documents and test results.

Summary: Define categories for medical documents
Description: Group items into categories such as blood tests, imaging, visit summaries and referrals.

Summary: Specify filters for document type, date and clinical area
Description: Determine filter options for quickly finding medical information.

Summary: Define metadata shown for each document or test result
Description: Determine fields such as document name, date, type and status.

Summary: Develop categorized medical test and document listings
Description: Implement an organized list of tests and medical documents.

Summary: Build a list of medical documents and test results
Description: Display all medical documents and test results, grouped by category.

Summary: Implement search and filtering controls
Description: Add search and filtering by date, type and medical field.

Summary: Allow users to open documents and results from the list
Description: Allow opening a document or result from the list.

Summary: Test results are displayed without their completion date
Description: Simulated defect scenario: a test result is displayed without its completion date.
Expected Result: Each item shows name, date and status.
Simulated Actual Result: Test results are shown without the date the test was performed.

Summary: Manage access permissions for sensitive medical information
Description: As a system administrator, I want to ensure that only authorized users can access medical information, so that patient privacy is protected and every access is traceable. The system will manage access to sensitive medical information by user type and role, so that only authorized parties can view it. Goal: protect patient privacy and meet information-security and medical-privacy requirements, which were defined as a key project constraint.
Acceptance Criteria: Define permissions for patients, physicians, other care professionals and administrators | Block unauthorized users from viewing sensitive medical information | Record access to medical information in an audit log | Reject invalid access attempts and display an appropriate message

Summary: Define a role-based medical-information access model
Description: Define an access policy based on user role and care relationship.

Summary: Define access rules for members, physicians, care teams and administrators
Description: Define permissions for member, physician, care provider and system administrator.

Summary: Define restrictions based on the patient's care relationship
Description: Allow access only to patients within the care provider's responsibility.

Summary: Review the access model with information security stakeholders
Description: Obtain approval from the information security department before development.

Summary: Implement access controls and medical-data audit logging
Description: Implement blocking of unauthorized access and logging of every view of medical information.

Summary: Block unauthorized users from accessing sensitive information
Description: Prevent access to medical information for unauthorized users.

Summary: Log access to medical information in an audit trail
Description: Record every view of sensitive medical information in an audit log.

Summary: Test invalid and unauthorized access attempts
Description: Run tests confirming that unauthorized users are blocked.

Summary: A user can access a medical document belonging to another member
Description: Simulated defect scenario (critical, access control): a user can view a medical document that does not belong to them.
Expected Result: Access is denied, an appropriate message is shown and the attempt is written to the audit log.
Simulated Actual Result: Member B's document is displayed to Member A.
